title: Reports Place Rybolovlev’s Jet Near Two 2016 Trump Campaign Stops
description_short: Flight-record reporting placed Rybolovlev’s jet near two Trump campaign stops in 2016; it does not establish that the men met or traveled together.
description_medium: A Philadelphia Inquirer report citing McClatchy flight records said Dmitry Rybolovlev’s aircraft landed in Las Vegas on October 30, 2016, when Trump held a rally there, and in Charlotte on November 3, near another campaign stop. The plane reached Charlotte less than an hour after Trump’s campaign aircraft. Rybolovlev’s representative denied contact. These movements do not prove the men met.
description_long: The Philadelphia Inquirer reported on flight records obtained by McClatchy that showed two airport overlaps between aircraft associated with Dmitry Rybolovlev and Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign. On October 30, Rybolovlev’s plane landed in Las Vegas on the day Trump campaigned there; the report said the jet spent about an hour and 20 minutes on the ground and taxied to a private hangar used by casino owner Sheldon Adelson. On November 3, Rybolovlev’s aircraft arrived at Charlotte Douglas International Airport less than an hour after Trump’s campaign plane, while Trump appeared at a rally in nearby Concord. Rybolovlev’s representative said the trip was for business and that he had no contact with Trump or his advisers. The reported records document aircraft movements and the representative’s denial. They do not establish that either man was aboard at the same time, that the two men met or communicated, or that the travel was coordinated. The evidence supports aircraft proximity only, not a personal meeting.

title: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_short: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_medium: The Associated Press reported that the new administration took down the White House Spanish-language website within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration; the Spanish-language X profile @LaCasaBlanca and a reproductive-freedom page were also disbanded. A White House spokesperson said the site was being edited and that archived content had gone dormant, and said the translation section would return. The evidence supports unavailability during the transition, not a permanent deletion claim.
description_long: Within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration, the White House Spanish-language homepage became unavailable and showed an error page. When asked about the changes, White House principal deputy press secretary Harrison Fields said the administration was developing and editing the website, that some archived content had gone dormant, and that it was committed to bringing the Spanish translation section back online. AP also noted that Trump had removed a Spanish White House page in 2017 and that the Biden administration restored it in 2021. These details distinguish the observed outage and account removals from an established permanent shutdown: the administration described the website status as transition work and promised restoration, though the report did not specify a date. The report describes the services as unavailable during the transition and says the administration expected the translation section to return.
